course.title: Khaemenes Academy Fifth Grade — Subject-Based 36 Week A++ Curriculum
course.subtitle: Advanced Upper Elementary Honors Foundation · In-House Curriculum · Subject Halls
course.dependencyPolicy: No outside fonts, scripts, images, libraries, or curriculum calls. All pages use local files only.
course.localReviewNote: Designed to exceed a single-state checklist by spanning broad Grade 5 academic, arts, health, technology, inquiry, research, capstone, portfolio, and middle-school readiness requirements. Local compliance review is still recommended.

subjects.title: Language Arts
subjects.description: Advanced Grade 5 literature, informational text, theme, comparison, point of view, text evidence, morphology, vocabulary, grammar, academic discussion, essays, research, revision, and publication.

subjects.title: Mathematics
subjects.description: Place value with decimals, powers of 10, multi-digit multiplication/division, fraction operations, decimal operations, coordinate planes, volume, measurement, data, and multi-step problem solving.

subjects.title: Science
subjects.description: Matter and its properties, conservation of matter, mixtures/solutions, Earth systems, water, stars, Sun/Earth/Moon patterns, ecosystems, energy flow, engineering, models, and evidence.

subjects.title: Social Studies
subjects.description: Geography, Indigenous civilizations, exploration, encounter, colonization, revolution foundations, constitutional principles, civics, economics, migration, rights, responsibilities, and informed action.

subjects.title: Arts & Music
subjects.description: Visual composition, design critique, rhythm, melody, notation foundations, dramatic interpretation, media arts, cultural arts, performance, artist statements, and portfolio curation.

subjects.title: Health, PE & SEL
subjects.description: Fitness planning, movement combinations, health decisions, nutrition, safety, wellness, emotional regulation, executive function, leadership, peer collaboration, resilience, and self-advocacy.

subjects.title: Technology & Tools
subjects.description: Keyboarding fluency, file systems, spreadsheets, data visualization, source notes, digital citizenship, accessibility, algorithms, debugging, presentations, ethical media, and computational thinking.

subjects.title: Integrated Projects
subjects.description: A++ studios where students research, calculate, model, test, write, build, revise, defend evidence, present publicly, reflect, and prepare for middle-school level expectations.

standardsFamilies.description: Quote accurately, compare themes and ideas, analyze text structures and point of view, vocabulary/morphology, grammar, discussions, opinion/informative/narrative writing, research, revision, publication, and presentations.

standardsFamilies.description: Decimal place value, powers of ten, multi-digit multiplication/division, decimal operations, fraction addition/subtraction/multiplication/division foundations, coordinate planes, volume, measurement, data, and problem solving.

standardsFamilies.label: Grade 5 Science and Engineering
standardsFamilies.description: Matter properties, conservation of matter, mixtures/solutions, ecosystems, energy flow, Earth systems, water, stars, Sun/Earth/Moon patterns, models, engineering, and evidence.

standardsFamilies.label: Grade 5 Social Studies and Civics
standardsFamilies.description: Geography, Indigenous civilizations, exploration/encounter, colonization, revolution foundations, constitutional principles, government, rights/responsibilities, economics, migration, trade, and informed action.

standardsFamilies.label: Arts and Music
standardsFamilies.description: Creative process, visual design, media arts, music literacy, rhythm, melody, drama, performance, critique, cultural arts, artist statements, and portfolio curation.

standardsFamilies.label: Health, PE, and SEL
standardsFamilies.description: Physical literacy, fitness planning, nutrition, safety, wellness, emotional regulation, executive function, collaboration, leadership, resilience, and self-advocacy.

standardsFamilies.label: Technology and Tools
standardsFamilies.description: Digital citizenship, keyboarding fluency, file systems, spreadsheets, charts, source notes, ethical media, algorithms, debugging, accessible presentations, and computational thinking.

standardsFamilies.label: Integrated A++ Projects
standardsFamilies.description: Cross-disciplinary inquiry, evidence gathering, data analysis, quantitative reasoning, research writing, modeling, design, revision, oral defense, portfolio, and reflection.

standardsFamilies.label: Portfolio and Assessment
standardsFamilies.description: Weekly mastery, performance tasks, midterm, final, capstone checkpoints, student reflection, teacher evidence, family reports, middle-school readiness, and 80% certification.

weeks.title: Fifth Grade Scholar Launch
weeks.theme: Baseline diagnostics, study systems, executive function, reading stamina, math fluency audit, inquiry notebooks, portfolio setup, and A++ expectations
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do fifth-grade scholars manage learning, evidence, revision, and responsibility?

weeks.title: Close Reading and Decimal Place Value
weeks.theme: Quoting accurately, decimal place value to thousandths, powers of ten, note systems, map precision, and learning evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does precision improve reading, math, and thinking?

weeks.title: Theme, Comparison, and Powers of Ten
weeks.theme: Theme comparison, characters/settings/events across texts, powers of ten, scale, and academic discussion
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do patterns help us compare ideas across texts and numbers?

weeks.title: Narrative Craft and Multi-Digit Fluency
weeks.theme: Narrative techniques, pacing, dialogue, sensory detail, multi-digit operations, and personal voice
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do strong choices help a writer or mathematician communicate clearly?

weeks.title: Decimal Operations and Real-World Problems
weeks.theme: Adding/subtracting/multiplying decimals, money contexts, estimation, and explanatory writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do decimals help us describe value and solve real problems?

weeks.title: Long Division and Remainder Decisions
weeks.theme: Division with two-digit divisors, interpreting remainders, procedural writing, estimation, and critique
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do we decide what a remainder means in context?

weeks.title: Fractions with Unlike Denominators
weeks.theme: Equivalent fractions, adding/subtracting unlike denominators, fraction models, and precision language
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can unlike parts be made comparable?

weeks.title: Multiplying Fractions and Scaling
weeks.theme: Fraction multiplication, scaling, area models, measurement contexts, and model-based explanation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can multiplication describe scaling and part-of-a-part thinking?

weeks.title: Dividing Fractions Foundations
weeks.theme: Unit fractions divided by whole numbers, whole numbers divided by unit fractions, story models, and visual reasoning
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can a model make fraction division understandable?

weeks.title: Volume and Three-Dimensional Design
weeks.theme: Volume as cubic units, rectangular prisms, additive volume, nets, design constraints, and engineering records
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does volume help designers solve space problems?

weeks.title: Coordinate Planes and Data
weeks.theme: Coordinate graphing, ordered pairs, line graphs, data stories, map connections, and digital charts
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can coordinates and data reveal relationships?

weeks.title: Geometry Hierarchies and Classification
weeks.theme: Properties of figures, hierarchy of quadrilaterals, classification, proof language, and design critique
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do properties help us organize shapes and arguments?

weeks.title: Matter: Properties and Measurement
weeks.theme: Properties of matter, measurement, mass, volume, density foundations, observation, and descriptive language
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can properties help us identify and compare matter?

weeks.title: Conservation of Matter and Mixtures
weeks.theme: Conservation of matter, mixtures, solutions, separation methods, data tables, and CER writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can evidence show that matter is conserved?

weeks.title: Forces, Motion, and Data Arguments
weeks.theme: Forces, motion, variables, graphs, models, fair tests, mathematical interpretation, and technical writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does data help explain motion and change?

weeks.title: Earth Systems: Spheres and Water
weeks.theme: Geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, water distribution, maps, models, and human use
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do Earth systems interact and support life?

weeks.title: Midyear Portfolio and Assessment
weeks.theme: Cumulative review, midterm, essay conference, math defense, science notebook audit, and portfolio reflection
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can I prove growth across every subject?

weeks.title: Ecosystems and Energy Flow
weeks.theme: Food webs, producers/consumers/decomposers, energy flow, matter cycles, ecosystem models, and explanatory writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do energy and matter move through ecosystems?

weeks.title: Human Impact and Environmental Stewardship
weeks.theme: Natural resources, water/land choices, conservation, data, civic proposals, and ethical decision-making
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can evidence guide responsible stewardship?

weeks.title: Stars, Sun, and Scale
weeks.theme: Stars, apparent brightness, distance, scale models, informational reading, and mathematical reasoning
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can scale help us understand objects too large to experience directly?

weeks.title: Sun, Earth, Moon, and Patterns
weeks.theme: Day/night, shadows, seasons foundations, lunar patterns, data collection, and model evaluation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do patterns in the sky help us explain time and motion?

weeks.title: Indigenous Civilizations and Geography
weeks.theme: Indigenous civilizations, land, resources, culture, trade, primary sources, respectful historical language, and maps
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do geography and culture shape civilizations?

weeks.title: Exploration, Encounter, and Perspective
weeks.theme: Exploration, encounter, migration, trade, perspective, cause/effect, ethical history, and source analysis
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can we study encounters with accuracy, evidence, and respect?

weeks.title: Colonization, Regions, and Economies
weeks.theme: Colonial regions, resources, labor systems, trade, geography, economics, and comparative evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do geography, resources, and power shape economies?

weeks.title: Revolution Foundations and Civic Arguments
weeks.theme: Rights, representation, protest, revolution foundations, civic vocabulary, persuasive writing, and debate
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do ideas about rights and representation change history?

weeks.title: Constitutional Principles and Government
weeks.theme: Constitution, separation of powers, federalism foundations, checks/balances, rights, responsibilities, and civic action
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do constitutional principles organize public life?

weeks.title: Economics, Budgets, and Financial Reasoning
weeks.theme: Budgets, income/expenses, saving, profit/loss, decimals, trade, scarcity, opportunity cost, and market ethics
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do people make wise choices with limited resources?

weeks.title: Research Writing: Question to Thesis
weeks.theme: Research questions, source evaluation, paraphrase, citation notes, outline, thesis, evidence paragraphs, and revision
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do researchers build trustworthy explanations?

weeks.title: Argument Writing and Public Speaking
weeks.theme: Claims, reasons, evidence, counterarguments, transitions, speaking skills, audience awareness, and respectful critique
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can a strong argument be both persuasive and fair?

weeks.title: Poetry, Drama, and Media Literacy
weeks.theme: Poetry, drama, figurative language, media messages, performance, tone, structure, and artistic response
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do creators shape emotion and meaning through form?

weeks.title: Statistics Foundations and Data Stories
weeks.theme: Mean/median/mode/range foundations, data displays, line plots, interpretation, and written data arguments
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can data tell a story and still require careful interpretation?

weeks.title: Digital Citizenship, Spreadsheets, and Coding
weeks.theme: Digital safety, ethical media, spreadsheets, algorithms, debugging, charts, accessibility, and presentation design
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can digital tools strengthen evidence without replacing judgment?

weeks.title: Global Citizenship and Service Design
weeks.theme: Global interdependence, community needs, service planning, human dignity, resource choices, and informed action
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can local action connect to global responsibility?

weeks.title: A++ Big Question Capstone Research
weeks.theme: Independent inquiry, research plan, source notes, math/data component, science or civic model, and project schedule
weeks.essentialQuestion: What big question can I investigate with evidence, calculation, design, and care?

weeks.title: Capstone Studio, Revision, and Oral Defense
weeks.theme: Draft, revise, build, calculate, design, peer critique, presentation media, oral defense practice, and reflection
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can I make my evidence clear enough to defend?

weeks.title: Final Review and Middle School Readiness
weeks.theme: Cumulative final, portfolio defense, certificate, grade 6 readiness, study habits, reflection, and celebration
weeks.essentialQuestion: How am I ready for middle school?

requires: Weekly assessment average at or above 80%
Portfolio evidence approved by adult mentor
